question.text: The shortest wavelength of the Brackett series of a hydrogen like atom of atomic number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> is same as the shortest wavelength of the Balmer series of hydrogen atom, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Shortest wavelength of Brackett corresponds to n = 4 and n = ∞ and shortest wavelength of Balmer series corresponds to n = 2 and n = ∞
∴Z213.616=13.616⇒Z=2
